Adjusted response using Beige Book insights:

- Policy stance: The FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 0–0.25% and reaffirmed ongoing purchases of Treasuries and agency MBS/CMBS to support market functioning and credit transmission. Repo and ON RRP facilities remain in place. The Fed emphasized that the outlook depends on the virus and that risks to activity, employment, and inflation remain elevated.

- Beige Book corroboration: Districts reported slight-to-modest gains off very depressed levels. Consumer spending and autos rebounded from lows; manufacturing and freight improved but remained below pre-pandemic; residential housing demand strengthened. However, commercial real estate—especially retail and hospitality—remained weak, the energy sector was subdued, and labor markets, while improving, still showed high unemployment and reduced hours. Price pressures were muted.

- Credit conditions (Beige Book + SLOOS): Banks reported broad-based tightening in C&I and CRE lending standards and terms, and also tightened for most consumer credit. Mortgage demand was solid (refi and purchase), but standards tightened there too. Loan demand outside mortgages was generally weaker, and banks expected further tightening through year-end due to deteriorating outlooks and collateral values. This bank-intermediated tightening offsets some benefit from improved market functioning noted by the FOMC.

- Net assessment: The Fed’s strong accommodation and improved market functioning are positives, but Beige Book and SLOOS point to ongoing credit headwinds, sectoral weakness (CRE, energy), and high uncertainty. Overall tone remains cautiously negative despite signs of stabilization.
